title.es: Presente simple — la ventana de la identidad

coreIdea.en: Present Simple is the window onto what is generally, normally true — identity, habits, facts.
coreIdea.es: El presente simple es la ventana a lo que es generalmente cierto — identidad, hábitos, hechos.

text.en: Grammar books say Present Simple is 'for routines'. That is true, but it is not the whole truth. Its real job is to describe the world as generally, normally true — identity, habits, facts and opinions.
text.es: Los libros dicen que el presente simple es 'para rutinas'. Es cierto, pero no es toda la verdad. Su función real es describir el mundo como algo generalmente cierto — identidad, hábitos, hechos y opiniones.

text.en: The student's question: 'Am I describing my normal reality?' If yes, Present Simple is probably right.
text.es: La pregunta del estudiante: '¿Estoy describiendo mi realidad normal?' Si la respuesta es sí, el presente simple suele ser el correcto.

text.en: Stative verbs (know, believe, love, own, want…) describe states, not visible actions, so they normally avoid the continuous form.
text.es: Los verbos de estado (know, believe, love, own, want…) describen estados, no acciones visibles, por eso normalmente no van en forma continua.

examples.en: I work as an engineer.
examples.es: Trabajo como ingeniero.

examples.en: Water boils at 100°C.
examples.es: El agua hierve a 100°C.

examples.en: My brother lives in London.
examples.es: Mi hermano vive en Londres.

title.es: Presente continuo — el lente de acercamiento

coreIdea.en: Present Continuous zooms in on life while it moves — actions now and temporary situations.
coreIdea.es: El presente continuo hace zoom a la vida en movimiento — acciones ahora y situaciones temporales.

text.en: Present Simple sees the whole landscape; Present Continuous zooms in. It shows life while it is moving: actions now, temporary situations, trends, changing situations, and planned arrangements.
text.es: El presente simple ve todo el paisaje; el presente continuo hace zoom. Muestra la vida mientras se mueve: acciones ahora, situaciones temporales, tendencias, cambios y planes ya acordados.

text.en: 'I live in Bogotá' feels permanent (identity). 'I'm living in Bogotá' feels temporary — only the perspective changed, not the facts.
text.es: 'I live in Bogotá' se siente permanente (identidad). 'I'm living in Bogotá' se siente temporal — solo cambió la perspectiva, no los hechos.

text.en: The emotional continuous: with always/constantly/forever it stops being about frequency and starts being about feeling — usually irritation. 'He's always arriving late!'
text.es: El continuo emocional: con always/constantly/forever ya no habla de frecuencia sino de emoción — normalmente irritación. '¡He's always arriving late!'

examples.en: I'm learning Italian this year.
examples.es: Estoy aprendiendo italiano este año.

examples.en: Cities are becoming larger.
examples.es: Las ciudades se están volviendo más grandes.

examples.en: I'm meeting Sarah tomorrow.
examples.es: Me veo con Sarah mañana (ya está acordado).

title.en: Present Perfect — the bridge to now
title.es: Presente perfecto — el puente hacia el ahora

coreIdea.en: Present Perfect is a bridge from the past into now — not a real past tense.
coreIdea.es: El presente perfecto es un puente del pasado al ahora — no es un pasado de verdad.

text.en: Present Perfect is not really a past tense. It builds a bridge from the past into the present: 'this happened before, but I want you to think about now.' Use it for life experience, change over time, present results and unfinished time.
text.es: El presente perfecto no es realmente un tiempo pasado. Construye un puente del pasado al presente: 'esto pasó antes, pero quiero que pienses en el ahora.' Úsalo para experiencias de vida, cambios en el tiempo, resultados presentes y tiempo sin terminar.

text.en: A finished time word closes the bridge. 'yesterday', 'in 2018' → Past Simple. That is why 'I have seen him yesterday' is wrong; say 'I saw him yesterday.'
text.es: Una palabra de tiempo terminado cierra el puente. 'yesterday', 'in 2018' → pasado simple. Por eso 'I have seen him yesterday' está mal; se dice 'I saw him yesterday.'

text.en: BEEN vs GONE: 'I've been to Italy' = I visited and came back. 'I've gone to Italy' = I left and I'm still there.
text.es: BEEN vs GONE: 'I've been to Italy' = fui y regresé. 'I've gone to Italy' = me fui y todavía estoy allá.

examples.en: I've visited fifteen countries.
examples.es: He visitado quince países.

examples.en: I've lost my keys (I still don't have them).
examples.es: Perdí mis llaves (todavía no las tengo).

examples.en: Prices have increased a lot.
examples.es: Los precios han subido mucho.

title.es: Presente perfecto continuo — la cámara en time-lapse

coreIdea.en: Present Perfect Continuous is the time-lapse of the journey until now — the process, not the result.
coreIdea.es: El presente perfecto continuo es el time-lapse del recorrido hasta ahora — el proceso, no el resultado.

text.en: This tense answers: 'What has been happening over time until now?' It shows the journey, not the destination — ongoing activities, recent activity with visible evidence, repeated effort and temporary situations.
text.es: Este tiempo responde: '¿Qué ha estado pasando a lo largo del tiempo hasta ahora?' Muestra el recorrido, no el destino — actividades en curso, actividad reciente con evidencia visible, esfuerzo repetido y situaciones temporales.

text.en: Present Perfect shows the certificate (result); Present Perfect Continuous shows your tired hands (process). 'I've cleaned the kitchen' vs 'I've been cleaning the kitchen.'
text.es: El presente perfecto muestra el certificado (resultado); el continuo muestra tus manos cansadas (proceso). 'I've cleaned the kitchen' vs 'I've been cleaning the kitchen.'

text.en: Stative verbs stay in the plain Perfect: 'I've known her for years', never 'I've been knowing her.'
text.es: Los verbos de estado se quedan en el perfecto simple: 'I've known her for years', nunca 'I've been knowing her.'

examples.en: I've been studying English for three years.
examples.es: Llevo tres años estudiando inglés.

examples.en: You've been crying (your eyes are red).
examples.es: Has estado llorando (tienes los ojos rojos).

examples.en: I've been calling you all day.
examples.es: Te he estado llamando todo el día.

coreIdea.en: Past Simple just records what happened and pushes the story one step forward — finished events in finished time.
coreIdea.es: El pasado simple solo registra lo que pasó y empuja la historia un paso adelante — eventos terminados en tiempo terminado.

text.en: Think of a camera that simply films what happens. You are not interested in the background or the duration — you only want to tell the listener what happened next. Ask yourself: 'What happened next?' Each sentence moves the story forward.
text.es: Imagina una cámara que solo filma lo que ocurre. No te interesa el fondo ni la duración — solo quieres contar qué pasó después. Pregúntate: '¿Qué pasó después?' Cada oración mueve la historia hacia adelante.

text.en: In negatives and questions, 'did/didn't' carries the past and the main verb returns to its base form: 'She didn't buy it', never 'She didn't bought it.'
text.es: En negativos y preguntas, 'did/didn't' lleva el pasado y el verbo principal vuelve a su forma base: 'She didn't buy it', nunca 'She didn't bought it.'

text.en: For a life that has changed, English adds two extra tools: 'used to' (past states and habits no longer true — 'I used to live in Madrid') and 'would' (repeated actions inside a story — 'Every summer we'd visit my grandparents').
text.es: Para una vida que ha cambiado, el inglés añade dos herramientas: 'used to' (estados y hábitos pasados que ya no son ciertos — 'I used to live in Madrid') y 'would' (acciones repetidas dentro de una historia — 'Every summer we'd visit my grandparents').

text.en: A finished-time word (yesterday, last week, in 2020) forces Past Simple, not Present Perfect: 'I saw him yesterday', never 'I have seen him yesterday.'
text.es: Una palabra de tiempo terminado (yesterday, last week, in 2020) obliga a usar pasado simple, no presente perfecto: 'I saw him yesterday', nunca 'I have seen him yesterday.'

examples.en: I visited Rome last summer.
examples.es: Visité Roma el verano pasado.

examples.en: She arrived, sat down and started working.
examples.es: Llegó, se sentó y empezó a trabajar.

examples.en: The Second World War ended in 1945.
examples.es: La Segunda Guerra Mundial terminó en 1945.

title.es: Pasado continuo — la cámara de cine

coreIdea.en: Past Continuous puts you inside a past moment to watch the action unfold — the background, the scene, the interrupted middle.
coreIdea.es: El pasado continuo te mete dentro de un momento del pasado para ver la acción en desarrollo — el fondo, la escena, la mitad interrumpida.

text.en: Past Simple tells the event; Past Continuous paints the scene. With was/were + -ing it places us inside the moment and lets us watch it happen live. Ask yourself: 'What was happening at that moment?'
text.es: El pasado simple cuenta el evento; el pasado continuo pinta la escena. Con was/were + -ing nos coloca dentro del momento y nos deja verlo ocurrir en vivo. Pregúntate: '¿Qué estaba pasando en ese momento?'

text.en: The classic pair: a long action in progress (continuous) interrupted by a short, complete one (simple). 'I was cooking when the phone rang.'
text.es: La pareja clásica: una acción larga en curso (continuo) interrumpida por una corta y completa (simple). 'I was cooking when the phone rang.'

text.en: Use it for two simultaneous actions and for atmosphere: 'While I was cooking, my husband was setting the table.' 'The sun was shining and the birds were singing.'
text.es: Úsalo para dos acciones simultáneas y para la atmósfera: 'While I was cooking, my husband was setting the table.' 'The sun was shining and the birds were singing.'

text.en: Stative verbs (see, know, want…) avoid the continuous. 'I was seeing him yesterday' is wrong → 'I saw him yesterday.'
text.es: Los verbos de estado (see, know, want…) evitan el continuo. 'I was seeing him yesterday' está mal → 'I saw him yesterday.'

examples.en: At 8 p.m. I was studying.
examples.es: A las 8 p.m. estaba estudiando.

examples.en: I was cooking when the phone rang.
examples.es: Estaba cocinando cuando sonó el teléfono.

examples.en: The sun was shining and the birds were singing.
examples.es: El sol brillaba y los pájaros cantaban.

title.es: Pasado perfecto — la cámara de flashback

coreIdea.en: Past Perfect is already in the past and steps even further back — the earlier of two past events.
coreIdea.es: El pasado perfecto ya está en el pasado y da un paso aún más atrás — el más temprano de dos eventos pasados.

text.en: With had + past participle, this is a flashback: you are telling a past story and you jump to something even earlier. Ask 'Which event happened first?' — the earlier one becomes Past Perfect. Native speakers use it not for love of grammar, but because it removes confusion.
text.es: Con had + participio pasado, esto es un flashback: estás contando una historia en el pasado y saltas a algo aún más temprano. Pregunta '¿Qué evento ocurrió primero?' — el más temprano va en pasado perfecto. Los nativos lo usan no por amor a la gramática, sino porque elimina la confusión.

text.en: 'When I arrived, she had left' is perfectly clear (she left first). 'When I arrived, she left' is ambiguous — did she leave before or after?
text.es: 'When I arrived, she had left' es clarísimo (ella se fue primero). 'When I arrived, she left' es ambiguo — ¿se fue antes o después?

text.en: After 'had' use the past participle, not the past simple: 'They had gone home', never 'They had went home.'
text.es: Después de 'had' usa el participio pasado, no el pasado simple: 'They had gone home', nunca 'They had went home.'

text.en: It needs two past moments. Don't use it for a single finished event with a finished-time word: 'We had been in Paris last year' is wrong → 'We were in Paris last year.'
text.es: Necesita dos momentos pasados. No lo uses para un solo evento terminado con palabra de tiempo terminado: 'We had been in Paris last year' está mal → 'We were in Paris last year.'

examples.en: She had already left before I arrived.
examples.es: Ella ya se había ido antes de que yo llegara.

examples.en: I'd never seen snow before I moved to Canada.
examples.es: Nunca había visto la nieve antes de mudarme a Canadá.

examples.en: We couldn't enter because somebody had locked the doors.
examples.es: No pudimos entrar porque alguien había cerrado las puertas.

title.en: Past Perfect Continuous — the duration camera
title.es: Pasado perfecto continuo — la cámara de duración

coreIdea.en: Past Perfect Continuous measures how long an activity had been going on before another past moment — the duration, not the result.
coreIdea.es: El pasado perfecto continuo mide cuánto tiempo llevaba ocurriendo una actividad antes de otro momento pasado — la duración, no el resultado.

text.en: With had been + -ing, Past Perfect says something happened first; this says how long it had been happening. It often explains a past result. Ask yourself: 'Do I care that it happened, or how long it had been happening?'
text.es: Con had been + -ing, el pasado perfecto dice que algo ocurrió primero; este dice cuánto tiempo llevaba ocurriendo. A menudo explica un resultado pasado. Pregúntate: '¿Me importa que ocurriera, o cuánto tiempo llevaba ocurriendo?'

text.en: It explains a past result through duration: 'He was exhausted because he had been running.' The tiredness comes from the ongoing activity.
text.es: Explica un resultado pasado a través de la duración: 'He was exhausted because he had been running.' El cansancio viene de la actividad en curso.

text.en: Contrast: 'They had argued' (a completed action) vs 'They had been arguing' (the ongoing duration).
text.es: Contraste: 'They had argued' (una acción completada) vs 'They had been arguing' (la duración en curso).

text.en: Stative verbs stay in the plain Past Perfect: 'I'd known him for years', never 'I'd been knowing him.'
text.es: Los verbos de estado se quedan en pasado perfecto simple: 'I'd known him for years', nunca 'I'd been knowing him.'

examples.en: I'd been working there for ten years before I resigned.
examples.es: Llevaba diez años trabajando allí antes de renunciar.

examples.en: She'd been waiting for over an hour when the train arrived.
examples.es: Llevaba más de una hora esperando cuando llegó el tren.

examples.en: He was tired because he had been running.
examples.es: Estaba cansado porque había estado corriendo.

prompt.en: My brother ___ in London (it is his home).
prompt.es: My brother ___ in London (es donde vive).

why.en: London is his home — a stable, general truth, so Present Simple.
why.es: Londres es su hogar — una verdad estable y general, por eso presente simple.

prompt.en: Water ___ (boil) at 100°C.
prompt.es: Water ___ (boil) at 100°C.

why.en: A scientific fact / general truth uses Present Simple; third person adds -s.
why.es: Un hecho científico / verdad general usa presente simple; la tercera persona añade -s.

why.es: 'know' es un verbo de estado — no se puede 'ver' ocurrir, así que no lleva forma continua.

prompt.en: She ___ chocolate.
prompt.es: She ___ chocolate.

why.en: 'love' describes a state, not an action in progress → Present Simple.
why.es: 'love' describe un estado, no una acción en progreso → presente simple.

prompt.en: He never ___ (drink) alcohol.
prompt.es: He never ___ (drink) alcohol.

why.en: A habit / normal life uses Present Simple; third person singular takes -s.
why.es: Un hábito / vida normal usa presente simple; la tercera persona del singular lleva -s.

prompt.en: I ___ in Bogotá — just for six months.
prompt.es: I ___ in Bogotá — solo por seis meses.

why.en: 'just for six months' signals a temporary situation → Present Continuous.
why.es: 'solo por seis meses' indica una situación temporal → presente continuo.

prompt.en: Cities ___ (become) larger every year.
prompt.es: Cities ___ (become) larger every year.

why.en: A trend developing over time uses Present Continuous, even if nobody is doing it 'right now'.
why.es: Una tendencia que se desarrolla en el tiempo usa presente continuo, aunque nadie la haga 'justo ahora'.

prompt.en: I ___ on an exciting project this week.
prompt.es: I ___ on an exciting project this week.

why.en: 'this week' frames a temporary period → Present Continuous, not the general 'I work'.
why.es: 'this week' enmarca un periodo temporal → presente continuo, no el general 'I work'.

prompt.en: To sound annoyed about a habit: 'He ___ late!'
prompt.es: Para sonar molesto por una costumbre: 'He ___ late!'

why.en: Continuous + always adds emotion (irritation); 'always arrives' is a neutral observation.
why.es: Continuo + always añade emoción (irritación); 'always arrives' es una observación neutral.

prompt.en: I ___ (meet) Sarah tomorrow — it's already arranged.
prompt.es: I ___ (meet) Sarah tomorrow — ya está acordado.

why.en: A fixed future arrangement that exists now uses Present Continuous.
why.es: Un plan futuro fijo que ya existe ahora usa presente continuo.

prompt.en: I ___ him yesterday.
prompt.es: I ___ him yesterday.

why.en: 'yesterday' is finished time — it closes the bridge, so Past Simple.
why.es: 'yesterday' es tiempo terminado — cierra el puente, así que pasado simple.

prompt.en: I ___ Paris in 2018.
prompt.es: I ___ Paris in 2018.

why.en: 'in 2018' is a finished moment → Past Simple, not Present Perfect.
why.es: 'in 2018' es un momento terminado → pasado simple, no presente perfecto.

prompt.en: She isn't here — she ___ home.
prompt.es: She isn't here — she ___ home.

why.en: 'gone' = left and not back yet. 'been' would mean she went and returned.
why.es: 'gone' = se fue y aún no regresa. 'been' significaría que fue y volvió.

prompt.en: I ___ my keys — I still don't have them.
prompt.es: I ___ my keys — todavía no las tengo.

why.en: The result matters now (no keys) → Present Perfect. 'lost' would just be a finished story.
why.es: El resultado importa ahora (sin llaves) → presente perfecto. 'lost' sería solo una historia terminada.

prompt.en: Have you ever ___ (climb) a mountain?
prompt.es: Have you ever ___ (climb) a mountain?

why.en: 'ever' asks about life experience with no date → Present Perfect + past participle.
why.es: 'ever' pregunta por una experiencia de vida sin fecha → presente perfecto + participio pasado.

prompt.en: I ___ here since 2022.
prompt.es: I ___ here since 2022.

why.en: An activity from 2022 continuing until now → Present Perfect (Continuous). 'am working' can't express 'since 2022'.
why.es: Una actividad desde 2022 que sigue hasta ahora → presente perfecto (continuo). 'am working' no puede expresar 'since 2022'.

prompt.en: Your clothes are covered in paint! I ___ the room.
prompt.es: ¡Tu ropa está llena de pintura! I ___ the room.

why.en: Visible evidence of the process (paint on clothes) → Continuous; it may not even be finished.
why.es: Evidencia visible del proceso (pintura en la ropa) → continuo; puede que ni esté terminado.

prompt.en: I ___ her for years.
prompt.es: I ___ her for years.

why.en: 'know' is stative — it stays in the plain Present Perfect, never the continuous.
why.es: 'know' es de estado — se queda en presente perfecto simple, nunca continuo.

prompt.en: Great news — I ___ the report!
prompt.es: ¡Buenas noticias — I ___ the report!

why.en: A completed result (it's done) → Present Perfect. 'finish' is a moment, not an ongoing activity.
why.es: Un resultado completado (está listo) → presente perfecto. 'finish' es un momento, no una actividad en curso.

prompt.en: I ___ (study) English for three years.
prompt.es: I ___ (study) English for three years.

why.en: Duration + ongoing effort until now → Present Perfect Continuous.
why.es: Duración + esfuerzo continuo hasta ahora → presente perfecto continuo.

prompt.en: I ___ him yesterday.
prompt.es: I ___ him yesterday.

why.en: 'yesterday' is finished time, so English uses Past Simple, not Present Perfect.
why.es: 'yesterday' es tiempo terminado, así que el inglés usa pasado simple, no presente perfecto.

prompt.en: She ___ a new laptop.
prompt.es: She ___ a new laptop (en negativo).

why.en: After 'did/didn't' the verb returns to its base form: didn't buy, not didn't bought.
why.es: Después de 'did/didn't' el verbo vuelve a su forma base: didn't buy, no didn't bought.

prompt.en: The Second World War ___ (end) in 1945.
prompt.es: The Second World War ___ (end) in 1945.

why.en: A historical fact in a finished period uses Past Simple.
why.es: Un hecho histórico en un periodo terminado usa pasado simple.

prompt.en: When I was young, I ___ football every weekend (but not now).
prompt.es: When I was young, I ___ football every weekend (pero ya no).

why.en: 'used to' marks a past habit no longer true; keep the -d in the positive form.
why.es: 'used to' marca un hábito pasado que ya no es cierto; conserva la -d en la forma afirmativa.

prompt.en: She arrived, ___ (sit) down and started working.
prompt.es: She arrived, ___ (sit) down and started working.

why.en: A sequence of completed events uses Past Simple; each verb moves the story forward.
why.es: Una secuencia de eventos terminados usa pasado simple; cada verbo mueve la historia hacia adelante.

prompt.en: I ___ dinner when the phone rang.
prompt.es: I ___ dinner when the phone rang.

why.en: The long background action takes Past Continuous; the short interruption stays Past Simple.
why.es: La acción larga de fondo va en pasado continuo; la interrupción corta se queda en pasado simple.

prompt.en: While everyone ___ (dance), the lights suddenly went out.
prompt.es: While everyone ___ (dance), the lights suddenly went out.

why.en: The ongoing action in progress uses Past Continuous (was + -ing).
why.es: La acción en curso usa pasado continuo (was + -ing).

prompt.en: The sun ___ (shine) and the birds were singing.
prompt.es: The sun ___ (shine) and the birds were singing.

why.en: Describing the background scene of a story uses Past Continuous.
why.es: Describir el fondo o la atmósfera de una historia usa pasado continuo.

prompt.en: While I was cooking, my husband ___ the table.
prompt.es: While I was cooking, my husband ___ the table.

why.en: Two long actions happening at the same time both take Past Continuous.
why.es: Dos acciones largas que ocurren a la vez van ambas en pasado continuo.

prompt.es: By the time we reached the station, the train ___.

prompt.es: They ___ home before us.

why.en: After 'had' English uses the past participle: had gone, never had went.
why.es: Después de 'had' el inglés usa el participio pasado: had gone, nunca had went.

prompt.es: I ___ (never/see) snow before I moved to Canada.

why.en: The experience came before another past event, so Past Perfect (had + past participle).
why.es: La experiencia ocurrió antes de otro evento pasado, así que pasado perfecto (had + participio).

prompt.es: I ___ (work) there for ten years before I resigned.

why.es: Enfatizar cuánto duró la actividad antes de otro evento pasado → pasado perfecto continuo.

prompt.es: It ___ all morning before the sun finally appeared.

why.en: The focus is the duration of the rain before a past moment, so the continuous.
why.es: El foco es la duración de la lluvia antes de un momento pasado, así que el continuo.
